description: 11e Hidden awareness (corpus findings F001/F002) and the F007 deep-strike denial radius, driven against the live game on the official 11e terrain layout (26 dense pieces). Player 1's Shield-Captain is teleported into the dense terrain area at (260,750) with its ranged-attack history cleared -- exactly the 13.09 state ('within a terrain area that contains one or more dense terrain features' AND 'did not make one or more ranged attacks during this turn or during the previous turn') -- and the Ork Battlewagon is placed 10 inches away as its ONLY legal target, so the whole shooting phase on offer is a chip shot into a T12 Sv3+ hull. Asserts, in order: (a) TerrainManager.is_model_hidden agrees the model is Hidden -- ENGINE truth, not the AI's opinion; (b) AIDecisionMaker._position_would_be_hidden reaches the same verdict from a synthesised probe model, which is the mechanism F001 needs to score a destination the unit has NOT moved to yet; (c) that probe returns FALSE on open ground, so the predicate discriminates rather than always answering yes; (d) F001 pays a movement bonus for the Hidden destination and exactly 0.0 for the open one; (e) F002 prices the two-turn forfeit above zero; (f) F007 derives the deep-strike denial radius from GameConstants.reinforcement_min_enemy_distance_inches() and gets 8 inches under 11e, not the 9 the AI previously hardcoded; (g) the PLAYER PATH -- clicking the real 'Suggest (K)' button runs the live AI and writes its reasoning into the left-hand game log, where the player can read that the unit is staying Hidden rather than trading two turns of untargetability for a chip shot; (h) the CONTROL -- replaying the identical decision with flags.shot_recently=true (Hidden already surrendered, so there is nothing left to protect) returns SHOOT, proving the hold-fire is caused by the Hidden state and not merely by the shot being poor. NOTE: as of 2026-08-06 the five behavioural weights ship OFF (neutral) because the benchmark did not support enabling them, so this scenario loads tests/bench_profiles/yt_findings_on.json to exercise them. Finally, (i) the SHIPPED-DEFAULT check: clearing that profile returns SHOOT and re-loading it returns SKIP_UNIT -- proving both that the shipped defaults really are neutral and that the profile really does enable the behaviour. A1 (2026-08-07) extends this scenario from the hold-fire BEHAVIOUR to the hold-fire DATA: the branch now emits a `hold_fire` decision record pricing hold-vs-shoot, asserted both ways -- chosen_index 0 on the chip shot into the T12 hull, and chosen_index 1 once the same target is made soft enough that the shot outvalues two turns of untargetability. It also asserts the SHOOT path's per-weapon records carry a real score_breakdown, which is what makes shooting regret computable at all.
